fields.title: Onsite, pre-go live training is conducted in dedicated training areas. There will be 1 training area for accounting + sales / F&I and 1 separate training area for parts + service. Conference rooms, break rooms and any space that are away from distractions are preferred. The only requirements are that there is internet connectivity and between 3-4 dedicated training PCs (each with a keyboard and a mouse). Configuring additional, applicable hardware for users to be trained on is also recommended (common examples below): Laser and impact printers Label printers for deal jackets, parts special order labels and vehicle labels Mobile devices for mobile repair order creation, parts scanning and vehicle barcode scanning iPads for F&I Menu and forms casting MICR printer for printing test checks. During our hardware/technology discussions and Strategy and Process meetings, we will partner with you to finalize these areas so that they will be ready for training in the weeks preceding go live. Your Tekion Implementation Manager will partner with you to finalize the arrangements and confirm the training schedule. To the right, please provide the areas of the dealership that you have in mind for these training rooms.

State Law - we must retain a permanent record of all of our vehicles.  It must list the acquired/disposition dates, vin, make, model (there's a column for stock#), buyer/seller information, and transaction prices. if we are able to utilize the system in Tekion that will start generating the next stock# if we could download the fields in the 'vehicle screen' to export as an excel at any time for the state that would be amazing.  With the way that we have it - we had a situation in WI where the owner of the excel spreadsheet parted ways with the company and all of that information had been deleted.  If there's a way that the system can automatically generate those records AND reduce the amount of manual time it takes to fill in those things, that would speed up productivity in several areas.

fields.title: Onsite, pre-go live training is conducted in dedicated training areas. There will be 1 training area for accounting + sales / F&I and 1 separate training area for parts + service. Conference rooms, break rooms and any space that are away from distractions are preferred. The only requirements are that there is internet connectivity and between 3-4 dedicated training PCs (each with a keyboard and a mouse). Configuring additional, applicable hardware for users to be trained on is also recommended (common examples below): Laser and impact printers Label printers for deal jackets, parts special order labels and vehicle labels Mobile devices for mobile repair order creation, parts scanning and vehicle barcode scanning iPads for F&I Menu and forms casting MICR printer for printing test checks. During our hardware/technology discussions and Strategy and Process meetings, we will partner with you to finalize these areas so that they will be ready for training in the weeks preceding go live. Your Tekion Implementation Manager will partner with you to finalize the arrangements and confirm the training schedule. Are there any state/province, federal or OEM specific reporting which is used daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly?
fields.rawValue:
Monthly IL reports their Vehicle Use Taxes and County Taxes.  Quarterly we report our Tire Taxes.  Yearly - We print off all of our New Car Invoices that are in inventory as of 12/31 to send as a zip file to our CPA for LIFO Adjustments at the end of the year.  

State Law - we must retain a permanent record of all of our vehicles.  It must list the acquired/disposition dates, vin, make, model (there's a column for stock#), buyer/seller information, and transaction prices. if we are able to utilize the system in Tekion that will start generating the next stock# if we could download the fields in the 'vehicle screen' to export as an excel at any time for the state that would be amazing.  With the way that we have it - we had a situation in WI where the owner of the excel spreadsheet parted ways with the company and all of that information had been deleted.  If there's a way that the system can automatically generate those records AND reduce the amount of manual time it takes to fill in those things, that would speed up productivity in several areas.

fields.title: Notes about the chart of account changes you would like to make:
fields.rawValue:
The chart of accounts that we were once on, for the most part, was in accordance to the OEM Financials.  It is being converted to a SCOA (Standard Chart of Account) for all stores to have all of the same account numbers - the only variances, of course, are the sale/cost accounts across the brands.  This is to be able to start standardizing accounting processes and schedules so reports can be ran at an overview level and not by individual stores. 

We do not want anyone other than myself (Marcia Young) and Daniel Randolph to have the accessibility to change account #s, schedules, Financial Mapping, Split Accounts, etc, so the consistency can be kept up with or changed as a whole.

Are there any state/province, federal or OEM specific reporting which is used daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly?
allFields.rawValue:
Monthly IL reports their Vehicle Use Taxes and County Taxes.  Quarterly we report our Tire Taxes.  Yearly - We print off all of our New Car Invoices that are in inventory as of 12/31 to send as a zip file to our CPA for LIFO Adjustments at the end of the year.  

State Law - we must retain a permanent record of all of our vehicles.  It must list the acquired/disposition dates, vin, make, model (there's a column for stock#), buyer/seller information, and transaction prices. if we are able to utilize the system in Tekion that will start generating the next stock# if we could download the fields in the 'vehicle screen' to export as an excel at any time for the state that would be amazing.  With the way that we have it - we had a situation in WI where the owner of the excel spreadsheet parted ways with the company and all of that information had been deleted.  If there's a way that the system can automatically generate those records AND reduce the amount of manual time it takes to fill in those things, that would speed up productivity in several areas.

allFields.rawValue:
The chart of accounts that we were once on, for the most part, was in accordance to the OEM Financials.  It is being converted to a SCOA (Standard Chart of Account) for all stores to have all of the same account numbers - the only variances, of course, are the sale/cost accounts across the brands.  This is to be able to start standardizing accounting processes and schedules so reports can be ran at an overview level and not by individual stores.

Are there any state/province, federal or OEM specific reporting which is used daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly?
fields.rawValue:
Monthly IL reports their Vehicle Use Taxes and County Taxes.  Quarterly we report our Tire Taxes.  Yearly - We print off all of our New Car Invoices that are in inventory as of 12/31 to send as a zip file to our CPA for LIFO Adjustments at the end of the year.  

State Law - we must retain a permanent record of all of our vehicles.  It must list the acquired/disposition dates, vin, make, model (there's a column for stock#), buyer/seller information, and transaction prices. if we are able to utilize the system in Tekion that will start generating the next stock# if we could download the fields in the 'vehicle screen' to export as an excel at any time for the state that would be amazing.  With the way that we have it - we had a situation in WI where the owner of the excel spreadsheet parted ways with the company and all of that information had been deleted.  If there's a way that the system can automatically generate those records AND reduce the amount of manual time it takes to fill in those things, that would speed up productivity in several areas.

fields.title: Notes about the chart of account changes you would like to make:
fields.rawValue:
The chart of accounts that we were once on, for the most part, was in accordance to the OEM Financials.  It is being converted to a SCOA (Standard Chart of Account) for all stores to have all of the same account numbers - the only variances, of course, are the sale/cost accounts across the brands.  This is to be able to start standardizing accounting processes and schedules so reports can be ran at an overview level and not by individual stores. 

We do not want anyone other than myself (Marcia Young) and Daniel Randolph to have the accessibility to change account #s, schedules, Financial Mapping, Split Accounts, etc, so the consistency can be kept up with or changed as a whole.
fields.decodedValue:

populatedFlatRows.rawValue:
Monthly IL reports their Vehicle Use Taxes and County Taxes.  Quarterly we report our Tire Taxes.  Yearly - We print off all of our New Car Invoices that are in inventory as of 12/31 to send as a zip file to our CPA for LIFO Adjustments at the end of the year.  

State Law - we must retain a permanent record of all of our vehicles.  It must list the acquired/disposition dates, vin, make, model (there's a column for stock#), buyer/seller information, and transaction prices. if we are able to utilize the system in Tekion that will start generating the next stock# if we could download the fields in the 'vehicle screen' to export as an excel at any time for the state that would be amazing.  With the way that we have it - we had a situation in WI where the owner of the excel spreadsheet parted ways with the company and all of that information had been deleted.  If there's a way that the system can automatically generate those records AND reduce the amount of manual time it takes to fill in those things, that would speed up productivity in several areas.

Monthly IL reports their Vehicle Use Taxes and County Taxes.  Quarterly we report our Tire Taxes.  Yearly - We print off all of our New Car Invoices that are in inventory as of 12/31 to send as a zip file to our CPA for LIFO Adjustments at the end of the year.  

State Law - we must retain a permanent record of all of our vehicles.  It must list the acquired/disposition dates, vin, make, model (there's a column for stock#), buyer/seller information, and transaction prices. if we are able to utilize the system in Tekion that will start generating the next stock# if we could download the fields in the 'vehicle screen' to export as an excel at any time for the state that would be amazing.  With the way that we have it - we had a situation in WI where the owner of the excel spreadsheet parted ways with the company and all of that information had been deleted.  If there's a way that the system can automatically generate those records AND reduce the amount of manual time it takes to fill in those things, that would speed up productivity in several areas.

Are there any state/province, federal or OEM specific reporting which is used daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly?
csvReadyRows.decodedValue:
Monthly IL reports their Vehicle Use Taxes and County Taxes.  Quarterly we report our Tire Taxes.  Yearly - We print off all of our New Car Invoices that are in inventory as of 12/31 to send as a zip file to our CPA for LIFO Adjustments at the end of the year.  

State Law - we must retain a permanent record of all of our vehicles.  It must list the acquired/disposition dates, vin, make, model (there's a column for stock#), buyer/seller information, and transaction prices. if we are able to utilize the system in Tekion that will start generating the next stock# if we could download the fields in the 'vehicle screen' to export as an excel at any time for the state that would be amazing.  With the way that we have it - we had a situation in WI where the owner of the excel spreadsheet parted ways with the company and all of that information had been deleted.  If there's a way that the system can automatically generate those records AND reduce the amount of manual time it takes to fill in those things, that would speed up productivity in several areas.
